pages.text: Frogs are amphibians. Many live near ponds and streams.
extras: Amphibians often need water when they are young.

images.alt: A red-eyed tree frog sitting on a leaf.
A pond with reeds and lily pads.

pages.text: A frog's strong back legs help it leap and swim.

images.alt: A frog gripping a leaf with its toes.

pages.text: Baby frogs begin as eggs in water. Then they hatch into tadpoles.
extras: Tadpoles start life with tails and no legs.

images.alt: Many frog eggs floating together in shallow water.

pages.text: Frogs come in many colors and patterns around the world.
extras: Bright colors can be a warning in some species.

images.alt: A bright blue and red poison dart frog on the forest floor.
A green frog with bright red eyes on a leaf.
